newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds constructive for now, eye 113-09.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds constructive for now, eye 113-09.

text.p: September T-bond futures will look constructive in technical terms on Tuesday and could push up to 113-09, technical analysts said.
But much will depend on fundamental factors, with a mass of U.S. data due later in the session, they said.

"For today technicals look like taking second place to fundamentals," said Andy Cossor, fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London. "But despite that, the technical picture for T-bonds is seen as being constructive at present."
At 1017 GMT, September T-bond futures were at 112-00 in automated trade, down 2/32 from Monday's Chicago settlement.
But Cossor said the new highs reached on Monday at 112-07 had not been confirmed by a new high in the 10-day momentum indicator.
"That suggests some caution would not be a bad idea for existing longs and makes some paring back of positions look advisable ahead of the figures," he said.
The U.S. data due include May consumer prices at 1230 GMT, and May industrial production and capacity utilisation at 1315 GMT.

"If the data are constructive then we will be looking for a swift move above yesterday's high to test resistance at 112-14 and a rally to the highs from February at 113-09. However, with daily oscillators starting to look overbought the ability of the market to sustain these gains...is starting to look a bit limited," Cossor said.
To the downside, Cossor noted support in the 111-16, 18 area from hourly charts.
"Then below there is short-term trend support at 110-29 on a daily trendline from the lows of May 29," he said.
Technical analysts at a European bank in London said T-bonds were likely to see short term resistance in the 112-00, 112-16 area.
"Support to any correction should be above 110-00," they said in a research note, although they also pointed out main trendline support running through 109-00.
At the short end, September Eurodollar futures were at 94.140, down 0.010 on the day.
